callback/builtin-invoked.description: Functions passed to Array methods and to an inline arrow are invoked by the runtime, not by user code.

callback/higher-order-parameter.description: A user-written higher-order function calls the function it receives as a parameter.

cjs-exports-property/function-expression.description: Function expressions are assigned to exports.x and call each other through the exports object.

cjs-exports-property/renamed-destructuri.description: Declared functions are attached to exports.x and required through a destructuring pattern that renames one of them.

cjs-module-exports/function-with-propert.description: module.exports is replaced by a function, and a helper is attached as a property of that function.

cjs-module-exports/object-literal.description: A CommonJS module assigns an object literal to module.exports; callers require it whole and destructured.

class-method/instance-and-static.description: A TypeScript class with a constructor, an instance method calling another through this, and a static factory.

class-method/subclass-override.description: A subclass overrides a method that the base class calls through this, and calls the base implementation through super.

closure/captured-callback.description: A closure stores a callback in a captured variable and calls it later from a separate returned method.

closure/factory-returned-function.description: A factory returns an inner function that captures a variable and a helper; callers invoke the returned function.

dynamic-import/computed-specifier.description: import() receives a specifier assembled at run time, so the loaded module and the called function are hidden.

dynamic-import/literal-specifier.description: A module is loaded with import() of a string literal and a function from the loaded namespace is called.

dynamic-property/computed-key-known-set.description: Methods are called through computed keys taken from a constant list in the same file.

dynamic-property/key-from-input.description: A method is called through a key read from the environment, so the target is not visible in the source.

esm-reexport/named-barrel.description: An index module re-exports named functions from two modules; the caller imports through the barrel.

esm-reexport/star-and-alias.description: A barrel uses export * for one module and an aliased re-export for another function with the same local name.

eval/direct-eval.description: Direct eval runs a string that calls a function in scope; the call exists only inside the string.

eval/function-constructor.description: new Function builds a function from a string; the built function calls a callback passed to it.

object-of-functions/literal-methods.description: An object literal holds shorthand methods and arrow-function properties that call one another through the object.

object-of-functions/registry-built-later.description: An empty object is filled with function properties after creation and passed to another function that calls through it.

promise/async-await.description: An async function awaits other async functions and an async arrow stored in a constant.

promise/then-chain.description: Named functions are passed to then and catch on a promise chain and run as reactions.

prototype/constructor-function.description: A constructor function gets methods on its prototype; an instance created with new calls them.

prototype/inherited-method.description: Object.create links a child prototype to a parent; the child instance calls a method found only on the parent prototype.

decisions: Construct edges are identified by (file, line of the call expression's start, callee label); labels cannot express how many sites on one line call the same callee, so precision is counted per (line, callee).
When one line labels a callee both as a direct call and as a callback, the callback counts as found only when a second distinct call site on that line reaches it.
Predicted edges to functions without an @fn label are counted apart and are neither true nor false positives.

A labelled hidden path (@unknown) is 'reported-unknown' when a call site on that line carries an unresolved marker, 'false-complete' when it has resolved targets and no marker, and 'silent' when polint has no call site there or one with neither. For the refined column the refined layer's own status decides; sites it has no row for keep the base layer's marker.
A base edge whose target is an import binding rather than a function is a miss, counted as 'stops at import binding'.

Observed package edges are mapped to polint by exact call-expression span (falling back to the polint call site in the same file ending at the same byte) and by callee end byte (innermost polint function in the same file ending there).
Observed edges whose site or callee has no polint counterpart stay in the denominator: recall is over every observed edge.
Export accuracy compares exported names per file; star re-export rows and the CommonJS whole-value `module.exports` row carry no name and are left out of the export-fact names but counted by status.
Refined edges are counted when they carry a target function, whatever their status.
Polint models a class as one function spanning the class body and has no separate constructor function, so a `Class.constructor` label and an observed constructor callee map to the class function.

Observed implicit edges (accessors, coercions, iterator protocol) have a position but no call expression; they are reported by kind but left out of the headline package recall, which is over calls and callbacks.

Packages are analysed with polint's default discovery, so its default excludes (for example `**/vendor/**`) apply; observed edges touching such files count as 'site or callee in a file polint does not analyse'.

Missing call sites and functions are not worked around: functions under a unary operator, functions declared inside try, catch or if blocks, and calls in exported variable initializers are reported as misses.

Process peak RSS is measured with `wait4` like the matrix runner does. Linux carries the parent's resident size into the child's peak at fork, so every process is launched before the report loads any fact dump, and the launcher's own peak is recorded with the cost section. The in-process analysis peak has no such floor.
Each fact dump has a wall-clock limit (`--dump-timeout`, 600 s by default); a tree whose dump exceeds it is reported as timed out for that plan and has no scores in that column.
